source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 25 (PDF 228-246, printed 228-246); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 25 (Ecology), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The study of the relationships of organisms with other organisms and with the environment is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: ecology is the study of the relationships of organisms with other organisms and the environment.

book_ref.quote: Ecology is the study of the relationships of organisms with other organisms and the environment

blocks.prompt: 2 The basic unit of biological classification is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: a species is the basic unit of biological classification.

book_ref.quote: A species is the basic unit of biological classification

blocks.prompt: 3 According to the definition of a species, its members, most importantly:

options.text: can interbreed to produce fertile offspring
live in the same geographic area

blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: a species shares similar physical and genetic characters and, most importantly, can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

book_ref.quote: can interbreed to produce fertile offspring

blocks.prompt: 4 The book's example of a distinct species, whose members cannot breed with other types of dolphins to produce fertile young, is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: the Indus River Dolphin is a distinct species; all Indus dolphins breed with one another but not with other dolphins.

book_ref.quote: The Indus River Dolphin is a distinct species

blocks.prompt: 5 A group of individuals of the same species living in the same geographic area at the same time is a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: this is the definition of a population.

book_ref.quote: A population is a group of individuals belonging to the same species living in the same geographic area at the same time

blocks.prompt: 6 All the Markhors living in the Chitral Gol National Park form a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: Markhors in Chitral form a population; Markhors across all of Pakistan are referred to as the species.

book_ref.quote: all the Markhors living in the Chitral Gol National Park form a single population

blocks.prompt: 7 All the different populations of various species living and interacting in the same area make up a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: a community consists of all the populations of various species living and interacting in the same area.

book_ref.quote: A community consists of all the different populations of various species living and interacting in the same area

blocks.prompt: 8 In the book's example of a community, the Mangrove trees, mudskipper fish, crabs and shorebirds belong to a mangrove forest in:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: a Mangrove Forest in Karachi is the book's example of a community.

book_ref.quote: a Mangrove Forest in Karachi refers to a community

blocks.prompt: 9 In an ecosystem:

options.text: nutrients flow one way while energy cycles
energy and nutrients both flow one way
energy flows one way while nutrients cycle

blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: energy flows unidirectionally while nutrients cycle between the living and non-living parts.

book_ref.quote: In an ecosystem, energy flows unidirectionally while the nutrients cycle between the living and the non-living parts

blocks.prompt: 10 In the Thar Desert example of an ecosystem, which is an abiotic factor?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: snakes, blackbucks and shrubs are the community; the baking heat, shifting sand dunes and rare rainfall are abiotic factors.

book_ref.quote: the Thar Desert is a vast ecosystem

blocks.prompt: 11 A large, distinct geographical region characterized by its specific climate, soil, altitude and adapted plants and animals is a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: this is the definition of a biome.

book_ref.quote: A biome is a large, distinct geographical region characterized by its specific climate

blocks.prompt: 12 In Pakistan, the Coniferous Forest Biome is located in:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: the Coniferous Forest Biome is in the high-altitude areas of Murree and Swat, where cold winters and pine trees dominate.

book_ref.quote: Coniferous Forest Biome is located in the high-altitude areas of Murree and Swat

blocks.prompt: 13 The highest and most inclusive level of ecological organization is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: the biosphere is the highest and most inclusive level; it is the global sum of all biomes.

book_ref.quote: The biosphere is the highest and most inclusive level of ecological organization

blocks.prompt: 14 The biosphere is often called the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.1: the biosphere is often called the 'Global Ecosystem', a thin envelope where land, water and air interact.

book_ref.quote: The biosphere is often called the "Global Ecosystem"

blocks.prompt: 15 Biogeochemical cycles are the cyclic movements of chemical elements between:

options.text: biotic and abiotic components of the ecosystem

blocks.explanation: Section 25.2: they are cyclic movements of elements such as carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and phosphorus between biotic and abiotic components.

book_ref.quote: between the living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components of ecosystem

blocks.prompt: 16 A massive component of the biosphere where an element of a biogeochemical cycle is stored for long periods is called a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2: a primary reservoir ('sink' or 'pool') stores the element for long periods.

book_ref.quote: A primary reservoir ("sink" or "pool") is a massive component of the biosphere

blocks.prompt: 17 Which is a sedimentary cycle?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2: sedimentary cycles (reservoir: Earth's crust) include the phosphorus, sulfur and calcium cycles.

book_ref.quote: Sedimentary cycles, in which the reservoir is Earth’s crust

blocks.prompt: 18 In gaseous cycles, the primary reservoir is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2: in gaseous cycles (nitrogen, oxygen, carbon, water) the reservoir is the air or the oceans.

book_ref.quote: Gaseous cycles, in which the reservoir is the air or the oceans

blocks.prompt: 19 The hydrological cycle is another name for the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: the water cycle (hydrological cycle) is the continuous movement of water between abiotic and biotic components.

book_ref.quote: The water cycle (hydrological cycle) is the continuous movement of water

blocks.prompt: 20 The entire water cycle is powered by:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: the sun powers the entire water cycle; solar radiation heats surface water so it evaporates.

book_ref.quote: The sun powers the entire water cycle

blocks.prompt: 21 About what percentage of global evaporation occurs from the oceans?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: about 86% of global evaporation occurs from the oceans.

book_ref.quote: About 86% of global evaporation occurs from the oceans

blocks.prompt: 22 In Pakistan, the massive primary source of vapor that travels inland is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: the Arabian Sea is Pakistan's massive primary source of vapor.

book_ref.quote: the Arabian Sea serves as the massive primary source of vapor

blocks.prompt: 23 During condensation, clouds form when droplets:

options.text: cling to dust particles in the air

blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: as vapor rises and cools it forms droplets or ice crystals which cling to dust particles to form clouds.

book_ref.quote: These droplets cling to dust particles in the air to form clouds

blocks.prompt: 24 Sleet is:

options.text: rain mingled with snow or hail

blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: sleet is a rain mingled with snow or hail, one form of precipitation.

book_ref.quote: sleet (a rain mingled with snow or hail)

blocks.prompt: 25 The unconfined flow of water over the land surface when it can no longer infiltrate the soil is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: surface runoff flows into streams, rivers and eventually the oceans.

book_ref.quote: It is the unconfined flow of water over the land surface

blocks.prompt: 26 In Pakistan, infiltration:

options.text: recharges the aquifers used for drinking water

blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1 (tidbit): surface runoff feeds the Indus River, while infiltration recharges the aquifers we use for drinking water.

book_ref.quote: In Pakistan, surface runoff feeds the Indus River, while infiltration recharges the aquifers

blocks.prompt: 27 The major exit point of water from plants into the abiotic environment is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: transpiration is the major exit point; plants release water vapor through leaf stomata.

book_ref.quote: Transpiration in plants is the major exit point for water

blocks.prompt: 28 Water produced as a byproduct of respiration in plants and animals is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.1: respiration produces water as a byproduct; this metabolic water is exhaled as vapors.

book_ref.quote: This "metabolic water" is exhaled as vapors

blocks.prompt: 29 Nitrogen gas makes up about what percentage of the atmosphere?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere.

book_ref.quote: about 78% of our atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 30 Plants cannot use atmospheric N₂ directly because its atoms are joined by a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: N₂ atoms are joined by a strong triple bond which plants cannot break.

book_ref.quote: Its atoms are joined by a strong triple bond

blocks.prompt: 31 Conversion of N₂ into inorganic compounds like ammonia (NH₃) is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: nitrogen fixation converts N₂ into compounds like NH₃.

book_ref.quote: Nitrogen fixation is the process of converting N₂ into inorganic compounds like ammonia (NH₃)

blocks.prompt: 32 Which is a free-living (non-symbiotic) nitrogen-fixing organism?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: free-living fixers include cyanobacteria, Azotobacter and Clostridium; Rhizobium is symbiotic.

book_ref.quote: free-living (non-symbiotic) organisms (e.g., cyanobacteria or blue-green algae, Azotobacter, and Clostridium)

blocks.prompt: 33 Rhizobium fixes nitrogen while living in the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: Rhizobium is a mutualistic bacterium in root nodules of pulses like Chana and Moong.

book_ref.quote: mutualistic (symbiotic) bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium) present in the root nodules

blocks.prompt: 34 In atmospheric fixation, the energy to combine nitrogen with oxygen comes from:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: during rains and storms, lightning combines N₂ with O₂ into nitrogen oxides and then nitrates.

book_ref.quote: lightning provides the massive energy needed to combine atmospheric nitrogen with oxygen

blocks.prompt: 35 Atmospheric fixation fixes only about:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: only a small amount (5-10%) of nitrogen is fixed by lightning.

book_ref.quote: Only a small amount (5-10%) of nitrogen is fixed in this way

blocks.prompt: 36 The synthesis of nitrogen-containing fertilizers by combining atmospheric nitrogen and hydrogen is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: industrial fixation combines atmospheric nitrogen and hydrogen to produce ammonia.

book_ref.quote: The synthesis of nitrogen containing fertilizers is called industrial fixation

blocks.prompt: 37 Nitrosomonas converts:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: in nitrification, Nitrosomonas converts ammonia to nitrite (NO₂⁻).

book_ref.quote: Nitrosomonas convert ammonia to nitrite (NO₂⁻)

blocks.prompt: 38 The bacterium that converts nitrite (NO₂⁻) to nitrate (NO₃⁻) is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate, which plants absorb easily.

book_ref.quote: Nitrobacter convert this nitrite to Nitrate (NO₃⁻)

blocks.prompt: 39 Absorption of nitrates by plants and microbes to make proteins, DNA and chlorophyll is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: assimilation is the entry of nitrogen into the biotic world.

book_ref.quote: plants and microbes absorb nitrates from the soil and use them to make proteins, DNA and chlorophyll

blocks.prompt: 40 Decomposers converting organic nitrogen of dead bodies and wastes back into ammonia is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: ammonification is the recycling step done by fungi and bacteria.

book_ref.quote: They convert the organic nitrogen back into Ammonia

blocks.prompt: 41 Denitrification, the return of N₂ to the air, takes place mainly in:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: in waterlogged soils denitrifying bacteria (Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus) convert nitrates to N₂.

book_ref.quote: In waterlogged soils, denitrifying bacteria

blocks.prompt: 42 Thiobacillus takes part in the nitrogen cycle by converting:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.2.2: Thiobacillus is a denitrifying bacterium converting nitrates back into N₂.

book_ref.quote: convert nitrates back into Nitrogen gas (N₂)

blocks.prompt: 43 Unlike the cycling of matter, the flow of energy in an ecosystem is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3: energy flow is unidirectional.

book_ref.quote: unlike the cycling of matter, the flow of energy is unidirectional

blocks.prompt: 44 Different feeding groups of organisms in an ecosystem are known as:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: feeding groups are called trophic levels.

book_ref.quote: the organisms are arranged in different feeding groups, known as trophic levels

blocks.prompt: 45 Trophic level 1 consists of:

options.text: green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria

blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: trophic level 1 is the primary producers.

book_ref.quote: Trophic level 1 consists of green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria

blocks.prompt: 46 A rabbit feeding directly on producers belongs to trophic level:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: trophic level 2 is primary consumers (herbivores), e.g., insects, rabbit.

book_ref.quote: Trophic level 2 consists of primary consumers (herbivores)

blocks.prompt: 47 Besides secondary consumers (carnivores), trophic level 3 also includes:

options.text: parasites of animals feeding on herbivores

blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: trophic level 3 is secondary consumers and parasites of animals feeding on herbivores, e.g., frog, snake.

book_ref.quote: and the parasites of animals which feed on the herbivores

blocks.prompt: 48 Which is the book's example of a tertiary consumer?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: trophic level 4 is tertiary consumers, e.g., wolf, hawk.

book_ref.quote: Trophic level 4 consists of tertiary consumers (animals that eat carnivores)

blocks.prompt: 49 Detritus is:

options.text: dead, decomposing plant and animal material

blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.1: decomposers and detritivores consume detritus and fecal matter; they feed on all trophic levels.

book_ref.quote: They consume detritus (dead, decomposing plant and animal material), and fecal matter

blocks.text: 25.3.2 The Loss of Energy between Trophic Levels

blocks.prompt: 50 About how much of the solar energy falling on producers is converted to bond-energy of organic matter?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.2: only about 1 to 2% of solar energy is converted to bond-energy by producers.

book_ref.quote: About 1 to 2% of the solar energy that falls on a first trophic level

blocks.prompt: 51 An ecosystem generally has:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.2: there are generally three or four trophic levels.

book_ref.quote: There are generally three or four trophic levels in an ecosystem

blocks.prompt: 52 If producers fix 10,000 kcal, tertiary consumers gain about:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.2: 10,000 → 1,000 (primary) → 100 (secondary) → 10 kcal (tertiary).

book_ref.quote: If tertiary consumers eat secondary consumers, they gain about 10 kcal

blocks.prompt: 53 Short food chains are more energy efficient than long ones because:

options.text: energy is lost as heat at each transfer, so fewer steps lose less

blocks.explanation: Section 25.3.2 (tidbit): energy is lost as heat at each trophic transfer, so fewer steps mean higher efficiency.

book_ref.quote: Short food chains (with a smaller number of trophic levels) are more energy efficient

blocks.prompt: 54 The statistical study of the characteristics of populations is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: demography is the statistical study of populations.

book_ref.quote: Demography is the statistical study of the characteristics of populations

blocks.prompt: 55 The most important feature of demography, directly related to a population's ability to survive, is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: population size is the most important feature because it relates directly to survival.

book_ref.quote: Population size is the most important features of demography

blocks.prompt: 56 The percentage of members of a group that are alive at a given age is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: this is population survivorship, shown by survivorship curves.

book_ref.quote: Population survivorship is the percentage of members of a group that are alive at a given age

blocks.prompt: 57 In which survivorship type do most individuals live their potential life span and then die rapidly in old age?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: Type I (convex) populations, e.g., humans and mammals.

book_ref.quote: Humans’ and mammals’ populations make type I survivorship

blocks.prompt: 58 Birds, lizards and rodents show which survivorship curve?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: Type II populations have a constant probability of death throughout life.

book_ref.quote: individuals have a constant probability of death throughout their lives

blocks.prompt: 59 Very high juvenile mortality but much lower adult mortality is shown by:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: Type III (concave) curves are shown by fishes and many invertebrates.

book_ref.quote: individuals experience very high juvenile mortality rates

blocks.prompt: 60 In the exponential growth model the population:

options.text: adds a constant number each generation
increases by the same ratio per unit time

blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: in exponential growth the population grows without limits by the same ratio per unit time.

book_ref.quote: the population increases by the same ratio per unit time

blocks.prompt: 61 The growth curve of the logistic growth model is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: logistic growth stabilizes at carrying capacity, giving a sigmoid or flattened S curve.

book_ref.quote: growth curves assume a sigmoid, or flattened S, shape

blocks.prompt: 62 The number of E. coli bacteria per milliliter in a test tube is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: population density is the number of individuals per unit area or volume.

book_ref.quote: Population density is the number of individuals per unit area or volume

blocks.prompt: 63 When high-density populations approach carrying capacity, severe competition leads to:

options.text: decreased birth rate and increased mortality risk

blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: severe competition decreases birth rate and increases the risk of mortality.

book_ref.quote: leading to decreased birth rate and increased risk of mortality

blocks.prompt: 64 Which dispersion pattern is not common in nature and occurs in some plants with wind-dispersed seeds?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: random spacing is not common; individuals do not interact strongly.

book_ref.quote: It is not common in nature

blocks.prompt: 65 Nesting penguins that maintain defined territories show:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: territorial animals such as nesting penguins show uniform dispersion.

book_ref.quote: such as nesting penguins, also exhibit uniform dispersion

blocks.prompt: 66 Clumped spacing is common in nature because individuals:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: clumping results from uneven resources; organisms prefer resourceful habitats.

book_ref.quote: Clumped spacing is common in nature

blocks.prompt: 67 Which is a limiting factor that determines carrying capacity?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: limiting factors are food, water, shelter, nesting sites, predators and diseases.

book_ref.quote: Carrying capacity is determined by "limiting factors"

blocks.prompt: 68 The smallest number of individuals required for a population to survive and persist is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: below the minimal viable size a population faces a high risk of extinction.

book_ref.quote: The minimal viable population size is the smallest number of individuals required

blocks.prompt: 69 In a very small population like the few remaining Himalayan Brown Bears, inbreeding leads to:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4: inbreeding causes genetic weaknesses and lower immunity against diseases.

book_ref.quote: like the few remaining Himalayan Brown Bears in Pakistan

blocks.prompt: 70 The global human population reached 8 billion in:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4 (box): it reached 8 billion in 2022; 9 billion is expected about 2037.

book_ref.quote: In 2022, it reached 8 billion

blocks.prompt: 71 Changes in technology since the early 1700s allowed humans to:

options.text: expand the carrying capacity of their habitats

blocks.explanation: Section 25.4.1: control of food supply, weapons and remedies allowed humans to expand carrying capacity.

book_ref.quote: These changes allowed humans to expand the carrying capacity of their habitats

blocks.prompt: 72 According to the 2023 census, Pakistan's population was:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4.1: the 2023 census recorded 241.49 million; growth rate 2.55% annually.

book_ref.quote: the last census in 2023 recorded Pakistan’s population to be 241.49 million

blocks.prompt: 73 Pakistan's official annual population growth rate is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4.1: the growth rate is officially 2.55% annually.

book_ref.quote: Pakistan’s population growth rate is officially recorded at 2.55% annually

blocks.prompt: 74 If all life on Earth is weighed, the largest share of biomass is made by:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.4.1 (box): plants make about 82%, bacteria about 13%, humans only about 0.01%.

book_ref.quote: the human population only makes up about 0.01% of the biomass on Earth

blocks.prompt: 75 Which is an impact of rapid human population growth listed by the book?

options.text: increased waste generation and elevated pollution

blocks.explanation: Section 25.4.1: impacts include habitat destruction, resource depletion, waste and pollution, climate change, deforestation and epidemics.

book_ref.quote: The rapidly growing human population is perhaps the greatest challenge to the future of the biosphere

blocks.prompt: 76 Greenhouse gases:

options.text: let heat escape freely to space
let sunlight in but stop heat escaping to space

blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: GHGs allow sunlight to pass but prevent heat escaping, keeping Earth warm enough for life.

book_ref.quote: These gases allow sunlight to pass through while prevent heat from escaping directly back into space

blocks.prompt: 77 The most significant greenhouse gas, released by burning fossil fuels and deforestation, is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: carbon dioxide is the most significant GHG.

book_ref.quote: It is the most significant GHG

blocks.prompt: 78 Enteric fermentation in cattle releases:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: methane comes from coal and gas production, livestock and agriculture.

book_ref.quote: by livestock (enteric fermentation in cattle)

blocks.prompt: 79 Synthetic greenhouse gases emitted from industrial processes such as old refrigerators and air conditioners are:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: fluorinated gases are synthetic industrial gases.

book_ref.quote: These are synthetic gases emitted from industrial processes

blocks.prompt: 80 According to the WMO, global atmospheric CO₂ rose from about 280 ppm before industrialization to:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5 (tidbit): CO₂ rose from about 280 ppm to 428 ppm in 2026.

book_ref.quote: It has elevated to 428 ppm in 2026

blocks.prompt: 81 According to the IPCC Report (2023), global surface temperature has increased, compared with 1850-1900, by roughly:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: roughly 1.1°C rise compared with the pre-industrial era.

book_ref.quote: global surface temperature has increased by roughly 1.1°C

blocks.prompt: 82 Pakistan contributes what share of global GHG emissions?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5 (tidbit): less than 1%, yet it is among the top 10 most vulnerable countries.

book_ref.quote: contributes less than 1% of global GHG emissions

blocks.prompt: 83 When atmospheric temperature crosses 50°C, the human body:

options.text: cannot adjust normal body temperature, causing fatal heatstroke

blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: above 50°C the body cannot adjust normal body temperature, leading to fatal heatstroke.

book_ref.quote: When atmospheric temperature crosses 50°C

blocks.prompt: 84 A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) is:

options.text: very heavy rainfall over a small area in a short time
a sudden release of water from a glacial lake when its natural dam breaks

blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: a GLOF is a sudden release of water from a glacial lake due to breaking of its natural dam; a cloudburst is sudden heavy rain over a small area.

book_ref.quote: A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) is a sudden release of water from a glacial lake

blocks.prompt: 85 Sea level rise threatens coastal areas of Pakistan such as:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.5: seawater intrusion in Thatta and Badin is turning fertile land into salty marshes.

book_ref.quote: the coastal areas in Thatta and Badin are threatened

blocks.prompt: 86 Because its geography ranges from the highest peaks to the Arabian Sea, Pakistan is described as a:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6: Pakistan's geography creates a 'miniature world' of ecological diversity.

book_ref.quote: It creates a "miniature world" of ecological diversity

blocks.prompt: 87 The forests are called deciduous because:

options.text: a cold winter causes trees to drop their leaves

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.1: distinct seasons with a cold winter cause the trees to drop their leaves.

book_ref.quote: including a cold winter that causes trees to drop their leaves (deciduous)

blocks.prompt: 88 Annual rainfall in the temperate deciduous forests of Pakistan is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.1: 750-1500 mm rainfall; temperatures 4°C to 30°C.

book_ref.quote: Moderate temperatures (4°C to 30°C); annual rainfall between 750 mm and 1500 mm

blocks.prompt: 89 The soil of the temperate deciduous forest is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.1: rich, grayish-brown soil with high organic matter (humus).

book_ref.quote: Rich, grayish-brown soil with high organic matter (humus)

blocks.prompt: 90 Which animal is key fauna of the temperate deciduous forest?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.1: key fauna are Rhesus monkey, black bear, leopard cat, wolves and birds.

book_ref.quote: Rhesus monkey (Macaca mulatta), Black bear, Leopard cat

blocks.prompt: 91 The most widespread terrestrial ecosystem of the plains in Pakistan is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.2: the tropical thorn forest is the most widespread plains ecosystem.

book_ref.quote: This is the most widespread terrestrial ecosystem of the plains in Pakistan

blocks.prompt: 92 The plants of the tropical thorn forest bear thorns to:

options.text: deter herbivores and reduce water loss

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.2: xerophytic plants have thorns to deter herbivores and reduce water loss.

book_ref.quote: xerophytic (drought-resistant) plants with thorns

blocks.prompt: 93 Annual rainfall in the tropical thorn forest is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.2: scanty rainfall of 200-750 mm; summer temperatures can reach 50°C.

book_ref.quote: Scanty rainfall (200 mm to 750 mm annually)

blocks.prompt: 94 Which is key flora of the tropical thorn forest?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.2: key flora are Prosopis cineraria, Salvadora oleoides, Capparis aphylla and Vachellia nilotica.

book_ref.quote: Prosopis cineraria (Jhand/Kandi)

blocks.prompt: 95 The houbara bustard and chinkara are key fauna of the:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.2: camels, houbara bustard, chinkara, golden jackal and gerbils live in the thorn forest.

book_ref.quote: Camels, houbara bustard, chinkara, golden jackal

blocks.prompt: 96 Alpine and sub-alpine meadows are high-altitude grasslands where:

options.text: the climate is too harsh for large trees

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.3: they are 'cold deserts' or grasslands too harsh for large trees.

book_ref.quote: where the climate is too harsh for large trees to grow

blocks.prompt: 97 The mean annual temperature of alpine meadows is:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.3: mean annual temperature 1°C-10°C; snow up to 6 feet.

book_ref.quote: mean annual temperature between 1°C and 10°C

blocks.prompt: 98 The snow leopard and marmots are key fauna of:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.3: alpine fauna include snow leopard, brown bear, ibex, musk deer, marmots, snowcock, monal and golden eagle.

book_ref.quote: Snow leopard, Himalayan brown bear, Himalayan Ibex, musk deer and Marmots

blocks.prompt: 99 The current status of alpine meadows is fragile because:

options.text: freshwater flow from the Indus fell
melting snow caps due to global warming alter their balance

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.3: they are highly sensitive to global warming, as melting snow caps alter the meadow's balance.

book_ref.quote: These areas are highly sensitive to Global Warming

blocks.prompt: 100 Salt-tolerant forests at the interface of land and sea, called 'The Forests of the Sea', are:
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.4: mangroves are often called 'The Forests of the Sea'.

book_ref.quote: Often called "The Forests of the Sea"

blocks.prompt: 101 Avicennia marina (Timmar) makes up what share of Pakistan's mangrove forest?
blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.4: Avicennia marina makes up 95% of the forest.

book_ref.quote: Avicennia marina (Timmar) makes up 95% of the forest

blocks.prompt: 102 The water of mangrove forests is brackish, meaning it is:

options.text: a mix of fresh river water and salty seawater

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.4: brackish water is a mix of fresh river water and salty seawater.

book_ref.quote: Brackish (a mix of fresh river water and salty seawater)

blocks.prompt: 103 Pakistan's mangrove forests are threatened by:

options.text: reduced freshwater flow from the Indus and pollution from Karachi

blocks.explanation: Section 25.6.4: threatened by reduced Indus freshwater flow and Karachi pollution; restoration projects have helped.

book_ref.quote: Threatened by a reduction in freshwater flow from the Indus and pollution from Karachi
